domains_hint: Extra names your apps answer on, added on top of your main domain — never instead of it. Each one becomes a Caddy label on every app, so it carries its own routing directives. Saving rewrites those labels and restarts every running app.
main_domain_hint: Set by this server in .env.app and routed by each app's own compose file. {app} never changes it — the domains below are added alongside it.
extra_domains_hint: Each entry adds one route to every app, on top of the one it already has. A host is a template, resolved when an app starts, so it follows this server if its address changes — the variables it can use are:
domains_empty: No additional domains. Apps answer on the main domain only.
directives_hint: Applied to the route generated for this host. TLS belongs to the domain, not to the app: use import = gateway_tls for a host served with this server's own certificate, and leave it empty for one that should get its own from Let's Encrypt.
domains_apply_hint: Not applied yet — saving rewrites every app's Caddy labels and restarts the running ones.
domains_applied: Saved. Running apps are restarting onto the new labels.
domains_duplicate: Two entries use the same host.
unlisted_store: This app comes from a store you have not added:
unlisted_store_hint: Only install it if you trust that source.
restore_from_backup_hint: Reinstalls the app on top of that backup's data and .env.
app_env_hint: The variables {app} passes into every app it installs — the domain, the network, the identity apps are seeded with. The comments in the file explain each one. An empty value means "not set": the key is skipped rather than passed on blank.
app_env_applies: Saved changes reach each app the next time it starts. Nothing is restarted here.
app_env_ignored: {app} sets these itself, per app — the values here have no effect:
backups_hint: Where your backups go, and every backup you have. A backup is made when you back an app up, when you uninstall one — uninstalling never deletes data, it archives it — and on the schedule below.
backup_destination_hint: The engine every backup is written to. Local keeps them on this server's disk; a remote engine sends them to a repository so they survive losing the server. Switching engines only changes where new backups go — the ones you already have stay listed and restorable.
user_data_hint: Everything in {source} except your apps' own data, which each app backs up separately — Documents, Downloads, Media and anything else you keep there.
user_data_empty: No backups of your files yet. The next scheduled run will make one.
user_data_interrupted: A restore of your files was interrupted and did not finish. Your files are currently a mix of the backup and what was there before. Restore again to finish the job.
user_data_interrupted_stamp: It was restoring the backup from {when}.
user_data_mode_copy_hint: Puts the files in {dest}, leaving everything you have now untouched. Best for getting a few files back.
user_data_mode_in_place: Replace my files with this backup
user_data_mode_in_place_hint: Puts your files back exactly as they were at that moment.
user_data_in_place_warning: Files you have added or changed since this backup will be deleted. Your apps and their data are not touched. This cannot be undone from here — but a backup of your current files is taken first, so it can be reversed by restoring that one.
user_data_excluded: Not included in the backup, and so not restored: {list}
user_data_in_place_ack: I understand my current files will be replaced
backups_orphan_hint: This app is not installed. Restoring a backup brings it — and its tile — back.
backups_scope_note: The engine in use keeps backups on the same disk as your apps, so they protect against a bad update or a mistaken uninstall — not against the disk failing. Choose a remote engine above for that.
backup_hint: A backup archives this app's whole folder: its compose file, its .env and its data. The app is stopped briefly so the copy is consistent, then started again.
backup_running: A backup is running — watch the app's tile for progress.
backup_empty: No backups of this app yet.
backup_restore_confirm: Replace this app with the backup? The current state is archived first.
backup_delete_confirm: Delete this backup? It cannot be undone.
backup_engine_unconfigured: The selected engine has no repository configured, so scheduled backups will fail.
backup_retention_hint: Older backups are thinned out rather than deleted outright: daily for a week, then weekly, then monthly.
backup_key_hint: Your backups are encrypted with a key held only on this server. Email yourself a copy and store it somewhere safe — without it, backups cannot be restored, and nobody can recover it for you.
